title: Fahavalo, Madagascar 1947
synopsis: Fahavalo — enemy in Malagasy — was the name given by French colonial authorities to those who rose in the uprising of March 1947. Malagasy veterans who had fought alongside France in the Second World War returned expecting independence; instead they were returned to indigène status and forced labour on colonial plantations. The uprising that followed was suppressed with great violence; its scale remains disputed. Marie-Clémence Andriamonta Paes travels to the sites of the rebellion to meet its last surviving witnesses, weaving their testimonies with previously unseen archival footage and the music of accordionist Régis Gizavo. Won the Documentaries of the World Award at the 42nd World Film Festival.
